title: Measurement validation and study design
text: **A product claim needs evidence matched to its meaning**

pages.title: Evidence required before a product claim
text: **A product claim needs evidence matched to its meaning**

Validation begins with a precise claim. “Measures an eligible endpoint zone diameter” and “detects resistance within two hours” require different evidence. The claim should identify the material, method, users, environment, output and decision. Its wording should not exceed the evaluated domain.
## Proposed evidence ladder

Engineering verification establishes whether specified functions work. Analytical evaluation addresses measurement performance. Workflow and usability studies assess the complete interaction with intended users. Clinical performance or outcome claims require the corresponding study and regulatory assessment. A successful demonstration cannot stand in for all these levels. [R26] [R35]
## Make evidence maturity visible

The proposed product record should distinguish demonstrated functions, qualified functions, proposed engineering and future research. An external paper can establish that an approach is scientifically plausible, but its results belong to that study. Historical prototypes and software demonstrations also need their own scope and verification records.

Before external use, each claim should have an owner, supporting evidence, limitations and a review date. When the product, method or intended use changes, the evidence relationship should be reassessed. This discipline allows ambitious research to remain visible while keeping the released product description accurate.

pages.title: Intended use and risk analysis
text: **Risk analysis connects failure to the decision it could affect**

The proposed risk process should examine hazards arising from incorrect measurement, identity errors, misleading interpretation, unavailable service and unsafe instrument behavior. It should consider normal use, foreseeable misuse and combinations of failures. A low average error rate does not resolve a rare but consequential failure mode. [R51]
## Start with a concrete sequence

For example, an incorrect plate association can lead to a technically accurate measurement being attached to the wrong case. Better segmentation would not mitigate that hazard. Identity verification, review context and export checks address different points in the sequence.
## Controls need evidence of effectiveness

A warning is useful only if the intended user notices and understands it in time. An interlock needs testing under the failure conditions it is meant to prevent. The assessment should also consider new risks introduced by the control, such as excessive false alarms or a recovery path that encourages bypassing checks.

The risk record should link hazards, controls, verification and residual-risk decisions. It should evolve with field findings and product changes. This compendium proposes the process and relevant failure classes; it does not claim that a complete product risk-management file or acceptable residual-risk determination already exists.

pages.title: Measurement validation design
text: **Measurement validation needs a prespecified comparison**

A zone-measurement study should define the measurand, reference process, eligibility criteria and analysis before examining the final results. The measurand includes the physical plane, boundary convention, units and method context. Without these definitions, two accurate observers may appear to disagree because they are measuring different features.
## Proposed study structure

The study should include representative plate appearances and independent reference assessment. It should separate development data from evaluation data and account for repeated measurements within plates or isolates. Reference uncertainty and reviewer disagreement should be retained rather than treated as zero.
## Challenge the useful range

The dataset should include measurements near interpretation boundaries, irregular zones and other difficult conditions within the proposed scope. A collection dominated by easy, clearly separated cases may conceal performance weaknesses that matter in practice.

Acceptance criteria should be justified against the intended method and decision, with relevant national evaluation guidance and standards consulted. They should not be copied from an unrelated instrument or selected after viewing the results. The proposed evaluation should report both numerical measurement behavior and the consequences of that behavior in the intended reviewed workflow. [R35]

pages.title: Reference methods and adjudication
text: **The reference process also has uncertainty**

An independent reference provides the basis for assessing a proposed measurement or classification. Its suitability depends on the question. A manual zone reading can assess a zone measurement, while an MIC prediction requires an appropriate MIC reference. A software model cannot validate itself by comparing with labels generated by the same model.
## Proposed reference governance

Reference assessors should use a defined method and have appropriate competency. Blinding to the investigational output should be used where feasible. Disagreements should follow a prespecified adjudication process that retains the original readings and reasons for resolution.
## A consensus is a process, not an infallible truth

Consensus can improve consistency, but it may still contain systematic error. Where possible, the study should examine reference repeatability and use independent checks appropriate to the measurand. Difficult cases should not be discarded solely because experts disagree.

The proposed data model should store reference values separately from routine reviewer corrections. A correction made during product use may be useful training material after assessment, but it is not automatically a research reference label. Keeping these roles distinct supports honest evaluation and makes later reanalysis possible when a reference decision is revised.

pages.title: Dataset representativeness
text: **Representativeness is a property of the intended domain**

A validation collection should reflect the conditions under which the product is expected to work. Relevant dimensions include organisms, antimicrobial combinations, media, plate geometry, image quality, sites, users and clinically important result ranges. A large dataset can still be narrow if most observations come from similar cases.
## Build a coverage matrix

The proposed study should map intended-use dimensions to available cases and identify gaps before model training and final evaluation. Rare but consequential conditions may need deliberate enrichment. Their prevalence in the evaluation collection should be reported so that overall metrics are interpreted correctly.
## More images are not always more independent evidence

Many images of one plate can help study temporal behavior or acquisition repeatability. They do not provide the same population evidence as the same number of independent isolates. The analysis should identify the biological unit and account for dependence among observations.

Data collection should preserve failed captures and unavailable results, because these influence real-world coverage. A model evaluated only on images that passed an expert selection process may appear more capable than it is in routine operation. The proposed product evaluation should therefore distinguish performance on accepted images from the complete workflow's ability to obtain an acceptable result.

pages.title: Site and temporal separation
text: **Separate development from evaluation at meaningful boundaries**

Training and test separation should prevent information about the evaluation outcome from influencing model development. Random image splitting is often insufficient when several images share a plate, isolate, patient, batch or acquisition session. The relevant grouping depends on the claim being evaluated.
## Proposed separation strategy

The development collection supports model fitting and exploratory decisions. A validation collection supports tuning and threshold selection. A final independent collection or prospective period assesses the frozen system. Site and temporal separation can challenge transfer beyond the conditions that shaped development.
## Document what the split actually tests

A held-out site can test some operational transfer, but it does not guarantee coverage of every new organism or instrument revision. A temporal split can reveal drift while still sharing many site-specific features. The report should state which forms of generalization the design supports.

The proposed software should retain dataset release identifiers and partition assignments. If a reference label changes, affected analyses should be traceable. Evaluation data should not quietly migrate into training while the same historical metrics continue to describe the revised model. New training releases require an appropriate new assessment of performance.

pages.title: Repeatability and reproducibility
text: **Repeatability and reproducibility test different sources of variation**

Repeatability examines variation under closely controlled conditions. Reproducibility examines variation when specified conditions change, such as instrument, operator, day or laboratory. Both are relevant to a measurement product, and neither alone establishes agreement with the correct value.
## Proposed variance study

A nested or crossed design can separate contributions from repeated capture, repositioning, operator and instrument. The design should reflect the permitted workflow and avoid attributing biological change to instrument variation when the same plate is observed over a period in which its appearance evolves.
## Use stable targets for instrument questions

Reference artifacts can help isolate optical and geometric variation. Biological material is needed to assess the complete measurement of real appearances. These studies answer complementary questions and should be reported separately.

The analysis should estimate relevant variance components and uncertainty, not merely report that repeated values look similar. A highly repeatable systematic bias is still an accuracy problem. Proposed acceptance should therefore combine repeatability and reproducibility evidence with independent reference agreement and clear operating limits. The resulting calibration and service requirements should follow the observed sources of variation rather than an arbitrary maintenance interval.

pages.title: Bias agreement and uncertainty
text: **Agreement needs more than correlation**

Two methods can be strongly correlated while differing by a clinically relevant offset or scale error. Measurement validation should examine differences in the reported units, their dependence on magnitude and the uncertainty of the reference comparison. A scatter plot alone can conceal systematic disagreement.
## Proposed analysis views

For paired diameters, calculate the difference between the investigational and reference measurements in mm. Examine its average, spread and relationship to diameter, organism, image quality and other relevant factors. Agreement limits require assumptions about the difference distribution and appropriate handling of repeated observations.
## Preserve reporting resolution

Rounding can change comparisons near a decision boundary. The system should retain the original measured value and the rule governing its reported form. Analysis should distinguish raw measurement behavior from the effect of rounding and categorical interpretation.

A suitable study should report confidence intervals and case counts for important subgroups. Pooled agreement may conceal a systematic problem in a smaller domain. The proposed product should restrict its qualified scope when evidence identifies such a limitation, rather than allowing a favorable overall average to override the unresolved subgroup result.
